# trees

> One Intent UI (IAP v0.1) document, rendered by a small IAP host built from the spec and its conformance fixtures, through two real bindings (HTML and terminal) and four CSS skins over the HTML binding.

- Live: https://trees.customer0.dev
- Source: https://github.com/acoyfellow/trees
- Based on: https://intent-ui.com (RFC: https://intent-ui.com/rfc) by Brayden Wilmoth

## What it shows

- The page is rendered from the document: validate() → load() (tool source replayed from a recorded call, JSONata normalize and views) → resolved tree → binding. No screen is hand-written.
- The host in src/iap/host passes 28 of 28 IAP v0.1 conformance fixtures (validate 9, render 7, change 7, intent 5). It was written from the spec and fixtures only, without reading the reference implementation.
- Clicking a PR row runs the `pr-details` intent. The first click materializes a template (simulated model call), the host validates it, stores it and sets an alias (document v3 → v4). Later clicks, and every other tree, resolve through the alias with no model call.
- The "Show diff" checkbox writes block /ui state; both bindings re-resolve and hide the column.
- The inspector shows the live document, validate() output and the resolved tree.

## Caveats

- The model call is simulated: it answers with the RFC §15 worked-example template.
- PR data is a fixed recorded tool call, not GitHub.
- Only two bindings are real (HTML, terminal). System 7, Swiss, LCARS and shadcn are CSS skins over the HTML binding's markup.
- Actions other than intent, close, navigate (logged, not followed) and bound checkboxes aren't wired. The fixtures don't test actions either.
